title: boundary_from_content: adversarial content can cause sign() to always return Err
description: sign.rs::boundary_from_content() derives the MIME boundary deterministically from SHA-256 of the content. An attacker who controls the content can compute the boundary string and craft content that contains it, causing sign() to return Err(MalformedInput) with no retry. The collision check correctly prevents a malformed MIME message, but returns an unrecoverable error. Using a random boundary (with collision detection + retry) would eliminate this denial-of-service vector. The current SHA-256 approach was chosen for test reproducibility, but this benefit can be preserved via a flag or by recording the boundary in the test fixture rather than deriving it at runtime.
